correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the finite integral: for standardized circular complex Gaussians the squared moduli have unit exponential margins, and their joint Laguerre generating function is 1/(1−|ρ|²uv). The log-squared-modulus coefficients are −1/k, so dividing by four gives the log-modulus covariance, including perfect correlation. The two angular averages then leave the factor 1/(8π). Cauchy–Schwarz bounds the normalized argument by one. Discrete summation by parts after x=nθ gives the uniform integrable bound C(1+|x|)^−2, while Riemann sums converge on bounded x uniformly in compact parameter sets. The integral is positive near x=0. At fixed midpoint m the numerator is independent of separation and the log of the denominator is strictly increasing for d>0 by positive variance under exponential tilting; symmetry gives evenness. Endpoint Laplace asymptotics give the denominator w(0)w(1)e^(2m+2d)/(4d²) to leading order. The integrated linear dilogarithm term is (1/4) times the weighted squared-profile integral divided by that denominator; the quadratic remainder is integrable and lower order by boundedness and Plancherel. Profile reversal cancels the real exponential factors and conjugates the numerator. At n=1 the exact formula gives π²/24 as a normalization check.
residual_risks: The checker reports bounded numerical tests, some with an explicitly truncated integral; it is not used to establish the limit. The theorem does not give a joint n,d asymptotic or a law for vanishing endpoint weights.
